title: This ‘Always’ Happens to Stocks in a Midterm Year (It’s Happening Again Now)
creator: MarketBeat
summary: MarketBeat host Bridget interviews Mark Chaikin of Chaikin Analytics on the midterm-year pattern and the current AI-led pullback. Chaikin argues, from 100 years and 24 midterm cycles, that markets typically bottom in mid-October in a midterm year and then rally, with a median gain of about 22% to the following summer peak, so pullbacks on AI-scare or geopolitical headlines are buying opportunities rather than a reason to exit. He says software has turned after its January-to-July collapse and features three software buys: Palantir, a defence, government and enterprise data disruptor pulled back from a high and stabilising, which he wants to own for the next 6–12 months ahead of 2 November earnings; ServiceNow, breaking out to a six-month high after an upgrade, consolidating workflow and customer support; and CrowdStrike, down a little over 10% in a week after roughly doubling year to date, as AI and agentic software expand the cyber threat surface. His favourite stock for 2027 is AMD, now down 18% in a week — a flip from his earlier conditional stance to an outright BUY, citing its 64-bit floating-point chip for scientific and medical research and PC processors overtaking Intel. No prices or targets were stated for any call. Passing mentions included Dell, HPE, Micron, CoreWeave, Adobe, Salesforce, Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet.

calls.thesis: Guest Mark Chaikin: BUY reiterated (his last MarketBeat call was BUY on 2026-09-30; no same-voice flip — the channel's interim HOLD on 2026-10-03 was host Bridget, a different speaker). Palantir is a disruptor in defence/government and enterprise data processing, pulled back after a recent new high and stabilising; 'a stock you want to own for the next 6 to 12 months' and 'a great buying opportunity here' into the midterm sweet spot.
calls.base_case: Midterm low has been seen (100 years / 24 midterms: market bottoms mid-October, median +22% to the following summer peak); pullbacks of 1-3 days are the entry, and he expects a new high within about a month.
calls.bull_case: Expects a blowout quarter on Mon 2 Nov earnings; commercial sales growing substantially alongside government, and contracts already baked in are hard to replace once embedded.

calls.thesis: Guest Mark Chaikin: BUY reiterated (was BUY on 2026-09-30 in his last MarketBeat appearance; no flip). ServiceNow is breaking out to a new 6-month high after an analyst upgrade, up ~6.5-7% on the day AI names fell; it consolidates customer-support/workflow systems at large companies and cannot easily be replaced, and its business is mostly corporate, not government.
calls.base_case: AI is being integrated into ServiceNow's own product offerings rather than marginalising it; shares have not yet recovered their Dec-Jan high.
calls.bull_case: The next earnings report 'is going to open people's eyes' to what big software firms can do once they incorporate AI into their software.

calls.thesis: Guest Mark Chaikin: BUY reiterated (MarketBeat's last explicit CRWD call was BUY by guest Pete Carmacito of Chaikin Analytics; the 2026-10-15 entry was UNCERTAIN — no flip). CrowdStrike has pulled back a little over 10% in the last week after roughly doubling year to date; 'very definitely' a buying opportunity and he expects it a lot higher by year end as AI adoption makes cybersecurity essential.
calls.base_case: Cybersecurity spending depends on corporate/government capex, which he expects to flow again once midterm uncertainty lifts; post-election gridlock is, in his view, good for corporate decision-making.
calls.bull_case: Agentic software on personal computers (he cites Meta's Muse agent launch and 500M+ downloads) puts home networks at risk and expands the threat surface CrowdStrike protects.

calls.thesis: Guest Mark Chaikin: his favourite stock for 2027, now an 'incredible buying opportunity' after an 18% pullback within a week from its high. Stance flip CONDITIONAL_BUY->BUY (condition met): his 2026-09-30 MarketBeat stance was to buy a 5-8% pullback rather than chase highs — the current 18% pullback more than meets that condition (channel's last explicit AMD call was also CONDITIONAL_BUY, 2026-10-15).
calls.base_case: If the market rallies 20%+ to a peak next summer, 'AMD's going to lead the market'; he is very bullish but gives no price or target.
calls.bull_case: New 64-bit floating-point chip essential for scientific/medical/energy/defence research that 4/8-bit LLM chips cannot do; its chip powers El Capitan, the largest supercomputer in the world; new PC processors have overtaken Intel as the innovator, helped by Meta's Muse introduction.
